title: Cutover conductor: KV-locking + preflight validators for multi-region private VPC cutovers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an orchestrator service plus Terraform wiring that performs deterministic inter-region cutovers for Private (VPC) deployments. Focus on a safe, reversible process for stateful services: KV-based distributed lock for leader election, preflight health and data-consistency validators, automated rollback gates, and a dry-run mode to run non-destructive rehearsals. This will be used for regular failover drills and ad-hoc DR exercises for customer VPCs.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can acquire a distributed KV lock across regions and gracefully yield on contention
Preflight validators (API health, KV replication lag, storage quorum) run and return pass/fail with actionable reasons
Terraform modules expose a single 'cutover_plan' resource that wires target region, validation hooks, and fencing config
Cutover supports dry-run mode that simulates traffic routing and emits a runbook draft without making infra changes
Automated rollback triggers on validator failure and provides audit trail and metrics in the Console
End-to-end test in CI that runs a simulated cutover against a sandbox VPC and validates observability signals
implementation_notes: Use etcd-cluster-backed KV (customer-managed in Private) with a lightweight adapter for lock semantics
Operator runs as short-lived Lambda-style job in Dedicated control plane for Private installs; sterilize credentials after run
Validators are pluggable scripts (python/bash) stored in S3 and executed on control-plane runners; results are JSON output to the Console
Cutover state machine: PRECHECK -> ACQUIRE_LOCK -> PROMOTE_TARGET -> SWITCH_TRAFFIC -> POSTCHECK -> RELEASE_LOCK (with timeout and forced-fail path)
All steps must emit structured trace events and token-level cost attribution for audit
playbook_steps: 1) Create cutover_plan Terraform resource pointing to target-region and validators
2) Kick off dry-run and review generated runbook output in Console
3) Schedule actual cutover during maintenance window with on-call and SRE present
4) Orchestrator performs preflight validators; if any fail, abort and provide remediation links
5) On success, acquire KV lock, promote target control-plane endpoints, update DNS/route53 with TTL low
6) Run postcheck validators for traffic correctness and latency SLOs
7) Release lock and close runbook, archive artifacts and metrics

test_plan: Unit tests for lock adapter with simulated leader churn
Integration test: dry-run against sandbox VPC (no infra changes) validates runbook output
End-to-end CI: simulated cutover with test traffic, verify postchecks and automatic rollback on validator fail
Chaos test: inject network partition between regions during ACQUIRE_LOCK and ensure graceful abort
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV lock starvation under noisy neighbor networks. Mitigation: adaptive backoff + bounded leader lease and opt-in staggered retries.
Risk: Validator false-positive causes unnecessary rollback. Mitigation: create multi-signal validators and require quorum of signals unless override is explicit.
Risk: Credentials used for promotion leaked in logs. Mitigation: ensure scrubber, short-lived creds, and KMS envelope encryption for artifacts.
notes_for_reviewers: Please validate the lock lease timing assumptions against real network conditions in Private installations (ask SRE to provide p95 latencies).
Security: confirm KMS key usage pattern is acceptable; we propose ephemeral keys scoped to cutover runs.
PM: confirm the abort messaging and remediation links included in runbook are sufficient for operator workflows.
